slides.title: Spoken Tutorial on Understanding API
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **Understanding API**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,
• Define what an **API** is.
• Explain its role in **AI** applications.
• Identify how an **API** acts as a messenger.
• Apply the **API** concept to a food delivery app.

slides.title: What is an API? The Restaurant Analogy
slides.narration:
What exactly is an **API**?
An **API**, or **Application Programming Interface**, acts as a messenger.
It connects your application with an **AI model**.
Think of it like a waiter in a restaurant.
You, the customer, give your order, or **prompt**, to the waiter, the **API**.
The waiter takes your order to the kitchen, which is the **AI model**.
The kitchen prepares your dish, the **AI response**.
The waiter then brings your dish back to you.
You don't need to know how the kitchen works.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a restaurant scene with a customer (application), a waiter (API), and a kitchen (AI model), showing the flow of order and food.

slides.title: Demo: Food Delivery App - Vague Approach
slides.narration:
Now, imagine building a food delivery app.
What if you built it without an **API**?
You would need to connect directly to each restaurant's system.
You would have to understand their unique databases.
You would handle every communication detail yourself.
This would lead to a very complex and difficult system to manage.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a food delivery app with multiple, direct, and complex connections to individual restaurant systems, indicating a tangled and inefficient process.

slides.title: Demo: Food Delivery App - Improved with API
slides.narration:
But here's where an **API** makes a difference.
With an **API**, your app sends a simple request to the restaurant's **API**.
This request specifies the order you want to place.
The restaurant's **API** then handles all communication with its internal system.
It retrieves menu items, places orders, and confirms delivery status.
This makes the entire process efficient and smooth.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a food delivery app connecting to a single, standardized restaurant API, which then efficiently manages communication with the restaurant's internal system.

slides.title: Demo: Food Delivery App - Vague vs. Improved
slides.narration:
Let's compare the two approaches.
The vague approach needs direct, complex integration with each restaurant.
The **API** improved approach uses a standardized interface.
This simplifies development and ensures scalability.
It allows seamless interaction with multiple restaurants.
All this happens through a single connection.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side comparison: On the left, a tangled network representing the vague approach; on the right, a streamlined connection representing the API improved approach.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined an **API** as a messenger between applications and **AI models**.
We used the restaurant analogy to understand this concept.
We also saw how **APIs** simplify complex interactions.
We demonstrated this with a food delivery application example.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now as an assignment,
Think about a weather app or a travel booking site.
Describe how **APIs** might be used in these applications.
Explain how they fetch and display information from various sources.
Compare the results.
